pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Upgrades B.G. Shirke Construction Technology to ‘IND A’/Stable, Limits Enhanced
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has upgraded B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) Long-Term Issuer Rating to ‘IND A’ from ‘IND A-’. The Outlook is Stable. The instrument-wise rating actions are as follows.
keyRatingDrivers:
Strong Credit Metrics: The upgrade reflects BGSCTPL’s net adjusted leverage (net adjusted debt/EBITDA  staying below 2.25x on a sustained basis. According to provisional FY17 financials, BGSCTPL reported gross interest coverage (operating EBITDA/gross interest expense) 2.93x (FY16: 2.81x) and net adjusted leverage of 1.27x (1.41x). The sustainability in credit metrics was on account of reduced term debt and stable EBITDA, in addition to the receipt of mobilisation advances in 4QFY17, which limited reliance on working capital debt. At FY17E, BGSCTPL’s total adjusted debt stood at INR7,412 million (FYE16: INR7,993 million). Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s credit metrics to be sustained over the near to medium term on account of healthy order execution.

Improved Operating Margin: EBITDA margin rose to 15.5% in FY17 from 12.6% in FY16, driven by improved control of site expenses and execution of high-margin projects, with EBITDA standing at INR3,919 million (INR3,817 million). Revenue moderated to INR25,299 million in FY17 from INR30,375 million in FY16 due to the delayed commencement of large housing projects awarded by Delhi Development Authority owing to deferred approvals. According to the management, the approvals were received in June 2017. Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL to post healthy revenue growth for FY18-FY20 on account of strong revenue visibility.

Robust-but-Concentrated Order Book: At end-June 2017, BGSCTPL had an unexecuted order of INR149 billion (INR121 billion at end-October 2015), which translates to 5.89x of FY17 revenue (3.98x of FY15 revenue at October-end 2015). The customer concentration, albeit moderated, remained high, considering Delhi Development Authority and Maharashtra Housing and Development Authority represented 49.8% (65.2%) and 20.4% (19.8%) of the order book, respectively.

Moreover, project concentration, albeit moderated, remained high, given the top 10 projects accounted for 60.8% (86.2%) of the order book by value. The quality of order book has improved, with slow-moving projects and projects where work is yet to start as a percentage of total order book reducing to 3% of unexecuted order book as at end-June 2017 (end-October 2015: 10%). Nevertheless, the company continues to have a strong competitive position in the pre-fabricated housing industry, with an established operating record of over 30 years. This benefits the company in terms of meeting pre-qualification criteria when bidding for new projects of similar types.

Adequate Liquidity: In FY17, cash flow from operations weakened to INR1,262 million (FY16: INR6,502 million) due to a rise in working capital requirements in 4QFY17 and an increase in loans and advances to related parties (INR2,258 million; INR1.741 million). However, liquidity was cushioned by the receipt of mobilisation advances. Cash balances remained high at INR2,416 million at FYE17 (FYE16: INR2,603 million).

BGSCTPL’s maximum use of fund-based working capital limits was 31.2% over the 12 months ended April 2017. The company has undrawn bank lines of INR8.8 billion for use in FY18. Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s debt service coverage ratio to remain comfortable at 1.25x-1.50x over FY18-FY20 for servicing debt repayments of BGSCTPL & Five Stars Bulkcarriers Pvt Ltd (FSBCPL).

Exposure to Group Entities: BGSCTPL has applied for the amalgamation of FSBCPL in FY17; the application is pending regulatory and lender approvals. BGSCTPL and group company Five Stars Shipping Company Pvt Ltd have jointly guaranteed FSBCPL’s loans (FYE17: INR3.30 billion; included in FY17 adjusted debt). The agency has consolidated the financial profiles of BGSCTPL and FSBCPL for future projections and eliminated the corporate guarantee.

FSBCPL reported INR581.8 million in revenue for FY17 (provisional) (FY16: INR902.1 million), with EBITDA loss standing at INR173.4 million (EBITDA positive INR178.6 million). The agency expects the weak operating profile of FSBCPL to marginally moderate consolidated EBITDA margin in FY18. The agency expects BGSCTPL to continue supporting FSBCPL in the near-to-medium term and BGSCTPL to continue providing financial support to Shirke Recreation Enterprise (‘IND BB’/Stable), the operations of which are yet to pick up. In FY17, loans and advances to related parties have increased to INR2,258 million (INR1.741 million; INR1,113 million).

Transfer of Oil and Gas Division Assets and Real Estate Venture: In FY16, BGSCTPL transferred the assets of its oil and gas division to a separate group entity and recognised loans and advances worth INR2,129 million. The division was engaged in the development of two wells in Andhra Pradesh for ONGC Ltd. The commercial operations of the division were delayed due to technical challenges and the absence of an offtake agreement.

In FY16, BGSCTPL envisaged the execution of an INR1.5 billion redevelopment project in Magathane (Mumbai). However, the project will be undertaken by a separate group entity to insulate BGSCTPL’s cash flows from future redevelopment projects undertaken. According to the management, BGSCTPL has invested about INR170 million in the project until date. Construction work commenced in 1QFY18. BGSCTPL will not make further investment in the project.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: A substantial diversification in the customer base and project segments while sustaining the credit metrics at the current level would be positive for the ratings.

Negative: Net adjusted leverage exceeding 2.25x on a sustained basis could lead to a negative rating action.
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1955, BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Shirke Group based in Pune, Maharashtra. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as Delhi Development Authority, Maharashtra Housing and Development Authority, and City & Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market. 

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance and leasing companies, managed funds, urban local bodies and project finance companies. 

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Reserve Bank of India and National Housing Bank. 

India Ratings is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.

For more information, visit www.indiaratings.co.in.
